purpose: The section.tech body of the two composed app stand-ins (/start, /auth): one real CSS section type in two genuinely different shapes, modelled as one section with two VARIANTS and a polymorphic content contract. The legal pages, which share the same DOM wrapper, were decomposed into content.legal-header + content.legal-chapter (same DOM, different purpose - R6).

oneOf.title: onboarding-cta
oneOf.description: The /start stand-in. COMPOSED, NOT MEASURED - there was no source page to transcribe. Its word budgets are the lengths of this project's OWN composed copy, not measurements of fourmula.ai.

titleLines.note: Exactly 2 lines; the second sits in a .u-fonts-50 span. Composed: "Get started" (2) and "with Fourmula" (2).

body.note: Composed: 24 words. NOT a measured copy budget.

oneOf.title: auth-form
oneOf.description: The /auth stand-in. COMPOSED, NOT MEASURED. It carries the project's single <form>, which is DELIBERATELY INERT and is pinned to the auth-inert-form asset role.

titleLines.note: Exactly 2 lines; the second sits in a .u-fonts-50 span. Composed: "Sign in" (2) and "to continue" (2).

body.note: Composed: 11 words. NOT a measured copy budget.

assetRole.note: PINNED to exactly this role. assets/asset-roles.json pins its generationPolicy to must-not-wire-up, and extraction/verify_all.py check [j] compares the VALUE, not just enum membership.

inputType.note: The source uses type="text", NOT type="email". Reproduced verbatim.

inert.note: MUST be true. The form has no action, no handler beyond onSubmit={(e) => e.preventDefault()}, no state, no network call, and nothing is read from or stored for the field. A generator must never give it a destination, a handler, state, storage or an analytics event.

content.note: POLYMORPHIC. Deliberately a oneOf of TWO FULLY INDEPENDENT schemas, each with its own complete properties / required / additionalProperties:false - NOT a shared base plus allOf patches. In JSON Schema draft-07 additionalProperties:false on a shared base is evaluated only against that base's own `properties` and cannot see properties a sibling allOf branch adds, so the shared-base shape would silently accept fields from the wrong variant.

contentMaxWordsTotalNote: No section-wide total is declared because the two variants have different shapes; per-field maxWords apply on every field of both.

evidence.note: EVIDENCE LEVEL DIFFERS PER VARIANT AND IS NEVER FLATTENED.

onboarding-cta.traits: two-line h1, one composed paragraph, two CTAs

constraints.verification: Checked against all 5 real templates: content.tech is the single body node of `app-onboarding` and `app-auth`, immediately after chrome.menu, and it appears in no other template. Derived by running extraction/classify_routes.py against the real JSX.

shapeDecision.question: Do /privacy-policy, /terms-of-service, /start and /auth share one page shape?
shapeDecision.howItWasDecided: By running a real classifier (extraction/classify_routes.py) over the actual JSX rather than by inspecting the grouping. All four routes produce the IDENTICAL node list [chrome.cookie-consent, chrome.header, chrome.menu, content.tech, chrome.footer, chrome.awards-badge], so a node-list-only grouping collapses 6 routes into 3 shapes. The classifier then compares STRUCTURAL SLOTS, which is what actually decides shape.

result./privacy-policy + /terms-of-service: slots {longFormProse, anchorIndex} -> ONE shared template `legal`. They differ only in tag COUNTS (12 vs 16 h2, 2 vs 0 tables), which is instance content, not shape.
result./auth: slots {ctaRow, inertForm} -> its own template `app-auth`. NOT merged with /start: it carries a real <form> node that /start does not, which is a different content contract and a compliance-relevant one.

shapeDecision.conclusion: 6 routes -> 5 templates. Only /privacy-policy and /terms-of-service genuinely share one.
shapeDecision.secondReasonNotToMerge: Even if the slots had matched, /privacy-policy and /terms-of-service are measured-scaffolding while /start and /auth are composed-not-measured. Merging them would launder the composed pages' evidence level into the measured pages' (MASTER-GUIDE 3.17).
shapeDecision.legalDecomposition: Revision 1.1: /privacy-policy and /terms-of-service still render through <section className="tech">, but measured at 1440px that one node was 6011px of a 6956px page (86%) and 6660px of 7605px (88%) - a whole legal document in one section. R6 requires a legal document to be decomposed by its own heading boundaries, so the legal template now uses content.legal-header + content.legal-chapter x12-16 instead of content.tech. Same DOM, different purpose.

motion.detail: section.tech has no motion hook of its own: no data-flash, no data-hero-text, no ScrollTrigger. The only motion on these four routes is the global chrome (header, menu, footer, cookie banner). The hover-stagger sweep applies to the CTAs through primitive.button-primary / -outline.
motion.reducedMotionFallback: Unchanged - this section has no motion of its own; only the CTA hover sweep is suppressed.
motion.reducedMotionFallbackKind: design-rule (the source ships NO prefers-reduced-motion handling for this section, so the fallback is prescribed by this repository, not mirrored)

responsive.base: single column, 8rem top offset, 2rem side gutters; the .tech__title override renders the .u-h3 element at type.h1 (5.5rem)
responsive.max-991px: the overridden title drops 5.5rem -> 4.5rem and body.lead stays 1.125rem
responsive.max-767px: the overridden title drops to 2.5rem and body.lead to 1rem

notes: /start and /auth pass NO preloader prop, so they inherit Layout's `preloader = false` default and have NO preloader. The docstring table in src/layout/Layout.jsx:14-18 lists only /, /privacy-policy, /terms-of-service and 404 - it omits /start and /auth entirely, which is why their preloader state had to be read from the real call sites (src/pages/Start.jsx:15, src/pages/Auth.jsx:17) rather than from the table. This corrects a claim in the build groundwork.
unbudgetedFieldsNote: None: every text field in both composed variants is budgeted. The legal body prose that used to be exempted here now lives in content.legal-header / content.legal-chapter.
